newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil up $1, Med enjoys fragile Asian support.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil up $1, Med enjoys fragile Asian support.

text.p: NWE gas oil edged up $1 a tonne on Tuesday but premiums for physical oil stayed unchanged amid thin demand.
German demand remained very poor and stocks across Europe high but some traders expected modest support from Singapore.
"The arb isn't quite open but it may be enough to help support the Med a bit," one said.
Discounts of up to $14 a tonne from the IPE mean traders could theoretically load large prompt Mediterranean cargoes around $147 fob and sell into Singapore at close to $166.

In northwest Europe barges and Russian cargoes were discounted about 25 cents and 50 cents to the IPE July contract respectively, little changed from Monday. The contract was up $1 a tonne at $161.25 at 1119 GMT having traded a narrow 75 cents range during the morning.
EN590 or diesel cargoes were still talked around $5 to $5.50 a tonne over the IPE for prompt delivery into Rotterdam. Swaps talked $4.50 over for July, $5 for August and $5.50 for September.
Stocks are around 20 percent above year ago levels in Europe and 13 percent above in the United States.
